messages:

Subject: Renewal - mid-year capacity bump and billing alignment

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. We expect an extra 30% burst in inference spend starting mid-September due to a new pilot. Our renewal comes up Nov 1 and our finance team wants predictable billing and a simpler invoice cadence. A couple of questions: 

1) Can Redwood bridge the Sept->Nov surge with a temporary uplift bucket that is credited against the Nov renewal?
2) If we take a higher committed bucket now, can we co-term the new capacity with our Nov renewal (not aligned to calendar months)?
3) Any discount bands for expanding committed capacity mid-contract vs at renewal?

Can you send options we can share with Procurement? Attaching a spreadsheet with current usage and projected pilot needs.

Thanks,
Danielle
Director of AI & Analytics
PulseHealth

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal - mid-year capacity bump and billing alignment

Danielle —

Appreciate the context and the forecast. Short answer: yes, we have a couple of practical paths. I pulled together three options below (high-level) that balance predictability, cost, and timing. I’ll attach a more detailed worksheet (sending in a follow-up).

Option A — Temporary bridge (no long-term commit):
- Add a short-term uplift bucket for Sept–Oct (monthly separate invoice).
- Usage above existing commitment billed at pay-as-you-go rate.
- We apply a one-time credit if you convert that uplift into committed capacity at renewal. Typical credit = 50% of uplift fees applied toward the new commitment for qualifying converts.

Option B — Mid-contract committed top-up (co-term at renewal):
- Purchase an add-on committed capacity now; it’s billed pro-rata to your chosen cadence.
- New add-on auto-co-terms with Nov renewal (so everything aligns to Nov 1).
- We can offer a mid-contract expansion discount tier (5–10% depending on size and term length).

Option C — Early annualize (annualize now, invoice smoothing):
- Annualize the pilot capacity into a forward commitment starting now, billed monthly but with a blended rate.
- This locks a larger discount (10–18%) but requires an amendment to the SOW.

Quick notes on procurement asks we often see:
- If procurement needs a single invoice cadence, Option B with co-terming is usually the simplest operationally.
- For renewals where customers want to preserve flexibility, Option A keeps obligations minimal.

I’ll drop a spreadsheet with numbers and a short SOW draft so your procurement team can review. Want to set a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:30am PT?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Answers inline below then a short worked example at the bottom.

- Proration formula (Option B):
  * Charge = (Monthly rate of add-on) * (days remaining in the billing period / total days in billing period).
  * When co-terming to Nov 1 we calculate prorated charge from effective date to Nov 1 then apply the remainder as credit on the Nov invoice if you convert to a longer term.

- Invoice smoothing (Option C):
  * We support 6- and 12-month smoothing for annualized purchases.
  * Minimum for 12-month blended band is typically a 12-month forward commit equal to at least 30% of current annualized usage; exceptions can be discussed.

- Amendment template & acceptance window:
  * Attached SOW stub includes standard amendment language and a 14-day review window.

Simple worked example (numbers illustrative):
- Add-on monthly list = $50k/month; effective Aug 15 -> Nov 1 (78 days out of 92-day quarter)
- Prorated = $50k * 78/92 = $42.4k billed for partial period.
- If customer converts that add-on to a 12-month commitment at renewal, we credit 50% of the $42.4k ($21.2k) toward the new commitment in Nov.

I’ll attach the SOW stub and an example invoice PDF. Happy to jump on your preferred time for a walkthrough.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW-attachment-stub.pdf, attachment: example-invoice-Aug-2026.pdf]

Danielle —

Attached is a short 2-slide summary and the pricing worksheet that shows the per-token equivalents for the two scenarios you asked about. Headlines: 

- Option B (Mid-contract add-on + co-term): per-token = $0.0018 (after 7% mid-contract expansion discount, prorated billing applied).
- Option C (Early annualize with 12-month smoothing): per-token = $0.0015 (after 12% blended discount; requires 12-month amendment).

Lock-in window on conversion for Option B: the converted add-on must remain for the remainder of the renewed term (i.e., once it converts on Nov 1 we treat it as part of the Nov renewal commitment; standard renewal term is 12 months unless you elect 24-month billing; early termination follows the SOW). In short: there is no additional separate lock beyond the renewed contract term.

Next steps: 
- If PulseHealth prefers operational simplicity and minimal upfront cash, Option B seems to be the best fit.
- If you want max unit-cost savings and can commit for a year, Option C is the lowest per-token cost.
